chapter: Boyhood scene: halls and dance music
title: Lawn parties and dance halls of the Seventh Ward
summary: He describes lawn parties and tries with the interviewer to locate halls by ward.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: take care of who they did. What were some of the dances you watched? What were some of the halls?

Well, there was quite a few lawn parties, lawns around there. At Pecan Grove on St. Claude between, St. Claude, on part of Boevin, which is a parlor which was once called Boevin, between St. Claude and Marais, there was a big old yard there. And these primitive people from down, I call them primitive because they were some other kind of colored people. They were from the Lowell, Louisiana, Seminard Parish in Ballard, in that part, in Lowell, Louisiana, near Ballard on the suburbs. They would give these lawn parties on Friday nights and Sundays, in this yard. They'd decorate up with Chinese lanterns, and they'd have a five or six feet of down, a regular neighborhood jazz band. And they'd ball in open air. And in the 7th Ward, there was quite a few halls there. I think there's more halls in the 7th Ward than any one. There's a lot of halls in the 6th Ward. You think so?
There's an artisan hall. Autocrat? Autocrat.
Coise of Green Hall. Army's in the 7th Ward, isn't there? No, that's my best ministry. 6th Ward. That's a 6th Ward. Italian Hall is in the 6th Ward, isn't there?
No, that's my best ministry. 6th Ward. That's a 6th Ward. Italian Hall is in the 6th Ward, too. 6th Ward, too.

That's my best ministry. Oh, yeah. But the way it happened, there's another hall, like, the night was, it was an independent hall, and then the, the Grand Union Hall. I don't know about it. I know that wasn't 6th Ward, too. There's a lot of halls I've collected in my material that nobody's ever heard of. There weren't any buildings. On 8th Ward Street, between Seminard and Ennett, there was a hall in that block. But it was torn down to make, you know, make the residents. But there was always something happening in that 7th Ward. Funerals, parades, every Sunday you could count on a 3 or 4 advertisements.
